gaps.sentence: They managed ___ the deadline despite the strike.
The teacher advised us ___ the essay twice.
gaps.explanation: advise + object + to-infinitive: advised us to check. (advise + -ing is possible without object: advise checking.)
too + adjective + to-infinitive: too young to stay.

gaps.sentence: I'm learning ___ the guitar at the moment.
gaps.explanation: learn takes the to-infinitive (learn how to play).

gaps.sentence: I didn't mean ___ you — it was a joke.
gaps.explanation: mean (= intend) takes the to-infinitive: didn't mean to upset. (mean + -ing = involve.)

gaps.sentence: My parents wouldn't let me ___ out that late.
gaps.explanation: let takes the bare infinitive: let me go (no 'to').

gaps.sentence: She admitted ___ the last train and had to take a taxi.
gaps.explanation: 'Admit doing' — confess to a past action takes the gerund.

gaps.sentence: It was kind of them ___ us a lift to the station.
gaps.explanation: 'It was kind of them to give …' — to-infinitive after the adjective.
